summary: Waren Spacefarer, a young pilot with ten credits, wants forty thousand to buy the Kestrel from Marta Okafor. He took a no-questions relief pilot job on the ore tug Grubstake for Captain Dren Vasko, promised six hundred credits on delivery to Vesta. After a rough undock he heard something alive knocking in the hold. When Ceres Customs ordered an inspection, Waren tried to comply; Vasko punched him and lied about a clamp fault, but the cutter is now docking to board. Vasko, furious, reaches for a locker by the hold hatch.

facts: Marta Okafor will sell the Kestrel to Waren for forty thousand credits.
Vasko promised Waren six hundred credits on delivery to Vesta.
Something alive knocks inside the Grubstake's sealed hold.
Ceres Customs is boarding the Grubstake.

recent.narration:
The tram drops you at Ceres Ring Port with your pilot's license in your pocket and ten credits on your chip. Your mother's flat, three decks down, already feels like another life.

Through the grimy window of Okafor's Used Hulls sits the Kestrel: a dented short-hauler with scorched intakes and good bones. Marta Okafor, grey braids and grease up to her elbows, follows your stare.

"Forty thousand and she's yours, kid. Not a credit less."

Behind you, the dock job board flickers. One posting blinks red: RELIEF PILOT NEEDED. ORE TUG. LEAVES IN ONE HOUR. NO QUESTIONS.

Ten credits. Forty thousand. Your hands already itch for a flight stick.
recent.picture: A lean young man in his early twenties with short dark brown hair, light stubble and keen grey eyes, wearing a worn olive flight jacket over a grey t-shirt, cargo pants and scuffed boots, stands in a busy industrial space station dock looking through a grimy window at a dented old short-haul spacecraft; beside him an elderly woman in her sixties, sturdy build, weathered dark skin, long grey braids, grease-stained blue coveralls. Harsh fluorescent light, flickering job board screen behind.

recent.action: Take the risky ore tug job
recent.narration:
The tug is called the Grubstake, and her captain, a wiry man named Dren Vasko, barely glances at your license. "Six hundred credits on delivery to Vesta. Fly straight, don't open the hold."

Undocking goes wrong right away. A docking clamp sticks, the tug lurches, and your head smacks the console. Through the ringing you hear a hollow knock from the hold. Ore doesn't knock.

Then the comm crackles: "Ore tug Grubstake, Ceres Customs. Hold position for inspection."

Vasko's hand lands on your shoulder, heavy. "Burn for the asteroid shadow, kid. Now."

The patrol cutter's lights swing toward you.
recent.picture: Cramped cockpit of an old industrial ore tug in space, a lean young man in his early twenties with short dark brown hair, light stubble, keen grey eyes, worn olive flight jacket over grey t-shirt, rubbing his forehead at the controls; behind him a wiry man in his forties, gaunt face, shaved head, hard pale eyes, stained brown work jacket, grips his shoulder. Red warning lights, patrol searchlights through the viewport.

recent.narration:
You key the comm. "Customs, Grubstake holding position—"

Vasko's fist cracks across your jaw before you finish. He rips the headset free and snarls into it: "Clamp fault, Customs. Sorting it now." Too late. The cutter's voice goes flat and official: "Grubstake, prepare to be boarded. Any burn will be treated as flight."

The cutter slides alongside, docking collar extending. Vasko stares at you, breathing hard, then at the hold hatch. The knocking starts again, faster now, like whoever is in there heard the word "boarded" too.

"You just cost me everything, kid," Vasko says quietly, and his hand drifts toward the locker by the hatch.

action: Unlock the airlock for the customs team
